source_text: Ad omnia me tibi respondisse, Iuliane, et omnia refellisse, quibus putasti et disputasti voluminibus quattuor credendum non esse originale peccatum, et concupiscentiam carnis non posse culpari sine damnatione nuptiarum; puto quod perspicis, si pervicax non sis. … audes insuper dicere, quod contra impios bella susceperis … Audes te agmini sanctorum Patriarcharum, Prophetarum, Apostolorum, martyrum, sacerdotumque miscere … Audes dicere, quod a Manichaeorum consortio vincaris
pass_a_gloss: That I have answered you to all things, Julian, and refuted all things, by which you thought and disputed in four volumes that original sin is not to be believed, and that the concupiscence of the flesh cannot be blamed without the condemnation of marriage; I think that you perceive, if you are not stubborn. You dare moreover to say that you have undertaken wars against the impious. You dare to mingle yourself with the troop of the holy Patriarchs, Prophets, Apostles, martyrs and priests. You dare to say that you are conquered by a consortium of Manichaeans.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “That I have answered you on everything, Julian, and refuted everything by which, in four volumes, you thought and argued that original sin is not to be believed, and that the desire of the flesh cannot be blamed without condemning marriage, I think you see, if you are not obstinate.”

“… You dare, besides, to say that you have taken up war against the ungodly … You dare to join yourself to the company of the holy patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs and priests … You dare to say that you are being overcome by a fellowship of Manichaeans.”

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
